To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AQP7 controls the accumulation of fat in adipocytes and the maintenance of glucose levels.
AQP7 is a key player in fat accumulation in mice.

1) adipocyte AQP7 regulates glycerol transport and triglyceride accumulation, 2) AQP7 regulates the size of fat cells, 3) AQP9 is a key factor in the development of insulin resistance, 4) AQP7 and AQP9 may act in concert in the regulation of glucose and lipid metabolism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of aquaporins in the pathophysiology of obesity and diabetes.
the role of AQP7 in the regulation of body fat accumulation and its possible involvement in the pathophysiology of obesity and type 1 and type 2 diabetic states.
the role of aquaglyceroporin AQP7 in the regulation of fat accumulation and glucose homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AQP7 gene deletion is responsible for obesity in the mouse model.
AQP7 is a key player in the regulation of lipid and carbohydrate metabolism.
the deletion of AQP gene in mice leads obesity, diabetes and other diseases, while its expression in adipocytes is associated to fat accumulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AQP7 is an adipocyte‐specific glycerol channel that regulates triglyceride accumulation in fat and glucose metabolism in liver and skeletal muscle.
the glycerol channel AQP7 is a key regulator of fat cell size and glucose homeostasis in mice.
AQP7 is a key player in the pathophysiology of obesity and diabetes and a potential target for the development of new anti‐diabetic drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the control of glycerol flux across the cell membrane by AQP7 is crucial to maintain fat mass homeostasis.
AQP7 is a key regulator of adipocyte glycerophospholipid metabolism.
the AQP7‐mediated control of glycerol permeation in the adipocytes is a key mechanism for the control of body weight.
